title.narrative: Lifesaving and resilience -building WASH and FSL intervention in Dar'a and Deir ez Zor governorates.

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtOxfam proposes a 12-month multisectoral humanitarian response in underserved communities of As-Sanamayn, Izra’, and Da’el sub-districts in Dar’a governorate, and Deir-ez-Zor city in Deir-ez-Zor governorate. The project aims to improve access to safe water, sanitation, food, and essential services for 110,480 vulnerable individuals, including returnees, IDPs, and host communities, in line with cluster priorities. All targeted areas are SHF-prioritized sub-districts with inter-sector severity level 4 and face increasing pressure on basic services due to recent returns and ongoing displacement. Oxfam coordinated with relevant sectors, local authorities, and humanitarian actors, including EPDC, TGH, PUI, and GVC, to ensure complementarity and avoid duplication.ltbrgtOxfam informed the intervention through assessments and consultations with communities, local authorities, and sector partners. In Dar’a, Oxfam will rehabilitate three boreholes, two in Mahjeh and one in Western Maliha, including solar systems, and upgrade water networks in Izra’ city to improve water access for 18,500 people. In parallel, Oxfam will address sanitation risks for 20,000 individuals by rehabilitating sewage systems in Izra’ and Da’el, reducing environmental and public health hazards.ltbrgtUnder the project, SHF will contribute, alongside other Oxfam funds, to the rehabilitation of a bakery in Izra’ town by installing a second production line. Daily bread output will increase from 8.3 to over 16 tons, benefiting 33,880 people through improved access to affordable bread. The bakery design includes gender-sensitive measures and accessibility for persons with disabilities and older people. Oxfam will also rehabilitate the bakery in Kafr Shams by installing a production line, a generator, and the required civil and electrical works. Established by the community in 2020, the bakery remains non-operational due to a lack of equipment. Once rehabilitated, it will produce up to 8 tons of flour per day, equivalent to around 8,800 bread packs, meeting the daily bread needs of approximately 35,200 people and reducing reliance on distant bakeries, including Ghabagheb, located 30 km away.ltbrgtIn Deir-ez-Zor, Oxfam will scale up its MPCA response. Through six rounds of assistance, 580 households, equivalent to 2,900 individuals, will receive support to meet urgent needs such as food, rent, and essential services. This builds on ongoing MPCA programming and aims to reduce the use of negative coping strategies while supporting local markets.ltbrgtThe integrated response contributes to both Envelope 1 and Envelope 2 of the allocation strategy by addressing acute needs through WASH, bread provision, and MPCA, while strengthening access to basic services and supporting safe and dignified returns. Sectoral activities are geographically and programmatically aligned. In Dar’a, WASH infrastructure rehabilitation complements bakery rehabilitation, improving public health and food access. In Deir-ez-Zor, MPCA complements ongoing WASH and food security interventions funded by other donors. Gender and protection considerations are mainstreamed across all sectors through inclusive targeting, community engagement, and monitoring frameworks.ltbrgtlt/pgt
